- **Footnotes section** at the bottom; not in TOC.
- **No CI badges, no \"Inspired by…\" line, no hard-wrapping.**

## 2. Differentiation from adjacent lists

I checked both lists you flagged and restructured the README to make the unique scope obvious on first glance ([commit `9cf3900`](https://github.com/Harsh9005/awesome-scientific-ai-tools/commit/9cf3900)):

| Aspect | [`0x11c11e/awesome-ai-research-tools`](https://github.com/0x11c11e/awesome-ai-research-tools) | [`ai-boost/awesome-ai-for-science`](https://github.com/ai-boost/awesome-ai-for-science) | This list |

Several blocking issues here, flagging them together so they are easier to address.

**Licence.** The repo is MIT-licensed. The manifesto explicitly requires Creative Commons, with CC0 strongly recommended. MIT, BSD, Apache, GPL, WTFPL, and Unlicense are all called out as not acceptable. This is the first thing to change.

`Consultancies & Service Providers` stretches what an Awesome list normally curates. The manifesto talks about "the best", and a list of consultancies tends to drift into a vendor directory — even with rigorous selection it is hard to verify that any given consultancy is the best the way you can verify a tool or a piece of legislation. Worth thinking about whether the section serves readers or just lists firms. If you keep it, an inclusion criterion in a section intro would help (specific AI Act case work? client references? recognised certification?).

The other thing is the h3 subsections sitting inside several h2 categories (`Regulation Text` inside `Official EU Sources`, and similar elsewhere). The TOC only shows h2 headings, so a chunk of structure is invisible to anyone scanning the contents page. Either promote the important h3s into the TOC, or fold them into a brief prose intro under the parent h2 so the visible structure matches the real one.

Small wording note. `Templates & Checklists` reads ambiguously. Templates of what, written by whom? A one-line intro under that heading would clarify the bar.

Move this to a Contributing section at the bottom or remove it. - **Banner image width is 100%.** `` renders at full container width. The guidelines say "Set it to a maximum of half the width of the original image" for high-DPI images. If the banner is high-DPI, set the width to half the original pixel width. - **Six single-entry sections.** - API (1 entry: LOLAPI) - AWS (1 entry: TrailDiscover) - M365 (1 entry: Microsoft 365 Application IDs) - macOS (1 entry: LOOBins) - Hardware (1 entry: LOTHardware) - DevOps (2 entries, borderline) Merge these into parent sections or add more entries. - **Off-topic entries.** - [AI Agent Index](https://aiagentindex.mit.edu/) is "a public database to document information about currently deployed agentic AI systems." This has nothing to do with Living off the Land techniques or tools commonly abused by attackers. - [Cloud Native Landscape](https://landscape.cncf.io) is a general CNCF cloud tools catalog. It's not a LOL resource. - **Descriptions are excessively long.** Many entries have multi-sentence descriptions of 40-65 words: - Azure IP Lookup: 65 words - Cloud Native Landscape: 59 words - LOLGlobs: 43 words - RogueApps: 51 words Awesome list descriptions should be one short sentence. Trim to the essential point. - **Typo.** LOLESXi description: "LOLESXi eatures a comprehensive list" should be "LOLESXi features." - **Section intro paragraphs are non-standard.** Almost every section opens with an explanatory paragraph ("Related to Application Programming Interfaces", "Related to cloud environments / services or SaaS apps", "Focused on endpoints", etc.). These are unusual for awesome lists. Consider removing them or condensing to a single line. - **Horizontal rules.** Two `---` separators (after the banner and after the TOC) are non-standard for awesome lists. - **Entry title uses `/`.** "LOL / Commonly Abused" with spaces around a slash is an unusual title format. - **0 of 4 reviews are substantive.** All four claimed reviews (#3962, #3999, #3960, #3952) are one-line comments about how many reviews the other PR author listed:

  github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/main/python/samples/getting_started/workflows
  github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/main/dotnet/samples/GettingStarted/Agents
  ...
  ```

- **"Related Technologies > Standards & Protocols" entries are generic.** OpenAPI, OpenTelemetry, and MCP are industry-wide standards, not specific to Microsoft Agent Framework. Including them inflates the list without adding subject-specific value.

- **Entry description mismatch with PR body.** The diff entry says "Open-source development kit for building AI agents and multi-agent workflows." but the PR body says "for .NET and Python." The PR body includes language-specific context that was dropped from the actual entry.

- **Community section has only 2 entries** (Discord and Reddit). Very thin for a section.

- **Heavy repetition of single blog authors.** Jamie Maguire has 4 entries in the blog section. While each is a separate post, this heavy representation of one author suggests breadth of curation is limited.

- **`## Contributing` heading may trigger lint TOC warning.** The `## Contributing` level-2 heading causes awesome-lint to flag "ToC missing item for Contributing." The guidelines say Contributing must NOT be in the TOC. Fix by removing the heading or using a non-h2 heading.

The topic fills a genuine gap in the awesome ecosystem — no existing list focuses specifically on AI/LLM evaluation. The content depth is impressive. A few issues to address before this can be merged:

**Non-standard list item format.** Every entry uses an inline shields.io badge prefix and bold link text:
```
- ![](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/confident-ai/deepeval?style=social) [**DeepEval**](…) - Description.
```
The required awesome format is simply:
```
- [DeepEval](…) - Description.
```
Inline badges in list items fall in the same category as CI badges — they add visual noise, are a maintenance burden (star counts change constantly), and break the consistent formatting expected across awesome lists. All ~130 entries would need to be reformatted.

**Dead links.** A few entries point to repositories that return 404 — at minimum `MetaTool` (`meta-llama/MetaTool`) and `RAGTruth` (`zhengzangw/RAGTruth`) no longer exist. These should be removed.

**Entry placement.** The diff shows the entry inserted between "AI in Finance" and "JAX" (alphabetically) rather than at the bottom of the Machine Learning sub-section, as required by the checklist.

**Horizontal rules.** The `---` separators between sections will likely trigger awesome-lint warnings. The convention is to rely on heading-based separation only.

**Minor:** The tagline uses "A curated list of…" which is redundant for an awesome list. Also, the `&` vs. "and" in headings is inconsistent ("Prompt Evaluation & Safety" but "Guides & Training" vs. "Community and Conferences" elsewhere).
